name: Selank

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Rat studies and lab tests, mostly in Russia

track.title: Phase I
track.line: No published Phase I trial found

track.title: FDA approval
track.line: Not approved; was in FDA Category 2 (withdrawn)

what.text: Selank is a chain of seven amino acids: Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro. It was made at the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences, with the Zakusov Institute of Pharmacology. FDA's records call it selank acetate (TP-7).

src.label: Volkova et al., Front Pharmacol, 2016
Vyunova et al., Protein Pept Lett, 2018
FDA, bulk drug substances that may present significant safety risks (Category 2 page)

what.text: It is a synthetic copy of tuftsin, a natural four-amino-acid piece (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg) of an antibody protein, with three amino acids (Pro-Gly-Pro) added to one end to slow its breakdown.

src.label: Volkova et al., Front Pharmacol, 2016

what.text: A 2022 review of peptide drugs developed in Russia lists Selank as one of 14 peptide products registered there, as an anti-anxiety drug.

src.label: Deigin et al., Pharmaceutics, 2022 (review of peptide drugs developed in Russia)

what.text: How it acts, according to lab and animal studies:

items.text: In rat brain membranes, it changed how GABA (the brain's main calming signal) binds to its receptors, in a way the authors liken to benzodiazepines.

src.label: Vyunova et al., Protein Pept Lett, 2018

items.text: In rats given it in the nose, it changed the activity of genes linked to GABA signalling in the frontal cortex within hours.

src.label: Volkova et al., Front Pharmacol, 2016

items.text: In lab tests on blood plasma, it slowed enzymes that break down enkephalins, the body's own opioid-like peptides.

src.label: Zozulya et al., Bull Exp Biol Med, 2001

what.text: These mechanisms come from lab and animal work. They have not been confirmed in people.

research.text: Human evidence: a handful of small Russian studies in anxiety, published in Russian, plus one brain-scan study in healthy people. No trial is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov. FDA says it lacks important safety information on selank in people.

research.title: Generalized anxiety and neurasthenia, 2008

facts.v: Zozulia AA, et al. Zh Nevrol Psikhiatr Im S S Korsakova 2008;108(4):38-48 (in Russian)
Selank compared with medazepam, a benzodiazepine; no placebo group
62 patients with generalized anxiety disorder or neurasthenia: 30 on Selank, 32 on medazepam
Hamilton and Zung anxiety scales, clinical global impression, and enkephalin breakdown in blood

research.found: The authors report similar anti-anxiety effects with both drugs, and say Selank also reduced tiredness and had a stimulating effect.

src.label: Zozulia et al., Zh Nevrol Psikhiatr, 2008

research.title: Anxiety and somatoform disorders, 2014

facts.v: Medvedev VE, et al. Zh Nevrol Psikhiatr Im S S Korsakova 2014;114(7):17-22 (in Russian)
Selank compared with phenazepam, a benzodiazepine. The abstract does not describe randomization or blinding.
60 patients with phobic-anxiety and somatoform disorders
anxiety, memory and quality of life

research.found: The authors report an anti-anxiety effect that lasted a week after the last dose, and a mild effect on thinking.

src.label: Medvedev et al., Zh Nevrol Psikhiatr, 2014

research.title: Selank added to phenazepam, 2015

facts.v: Medvedev VE, et al. Zh Nevrol Psikhiatr Im S S Korsakova 2015;115(6):33-40 (in Russian)
phenazepam alone compared with phenazepam plus Selank
70 patients with anxiety-phobic, hypochondriac and somatoform disorders: 30 on phenazepam alone, 40 on both
HDRS, CGI and Spielberger scales; side effects on the UKU scale; Stroop and verbal fluency tests; SF-36 quality of life

research.found: With Selank added, the authors report a faster effect on the HDRS and fewer phenazepam side effects, such as poor attention and memory, sedation and sexual problems.

src.label: Medvedev et al., Zh Nevrol Psikhiatr, 2015

research.title: Brain scans in healthy volunteers, 2020

facts.v: Panikratova YR, et al. Dokl Biol Sci 2020;490(1):9-11
one dose of Selank, Semax or placebo, with resting-state functional MRI before and 5 and 20 minutes after
52 healthy participants across the three groups
connections between the amygdala, the prefrontal cortex and the rest of the brain

research.found: Connections between the right amygdala and part of the right temporal lobe differed between groups. No clinical outcome was measured.

src.label: Panikratova et al., Dokl Biol Sci, 2020

research.text: A 2008 Russian study reported changes in blood cytokines (immune signals) in patients with anxiety and neurasthenia who received Selank for 14 days. Its abstract does not give the number of patients.

src.label: Uchakina et al., Zh Nevrol Psikhiatr, 2008

research.text: No Selank trial was found on ClinicalTrials.gov. The search returned 10 records, none of which tested Selank.

src.label: ClinicalTrials.gov search for 'selank'

research.text: A 2021 US pharmacology review called phenibut and Selank "poorly studied Russian drugs with GABAergic mechanisms" that are sold to US consumers as dietary supplements, and said drugs with GABA effects should be checked for abuse potential before public access.

src.label: Doyno and White, J Clin Pharmacol, 2021

us.text: Not FDA approved for any use. Selank acetate was in FDA's Category 2 (substances that may pose significant safety risks) before its compounding nominations were withdrawn. It is not in the HHS peptide policy of October 2026. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: none. Drugs@FDA lists no Selank product.

items.text: FDA lists "Selank acetate (TP-7)" among substances that were in Category 2 whose nominations were withdrawn. FDA says compounded selank acetate "may pose risk for immunogenicity for certain routes of administration due to the potential for aggregation and peptide-related impurities" and that "FDA lacks important information regarding any safety issues raised by selank acetate administered to humans."

world.lead: Selank is a registered medicine in Russia, according to a 2022 review of Russian peptide drugs. No approval was found in the US, Canada or the EU. WADA does not name it.

after.text: Selank is not named on the WADA Prohibited List for 2026 or 2027. WADA class S0 bans at all times any pharmacological substance not covered by another class and with no current approval by any government health authority for human therapeutic use. For 2027, WADA adds "peptides" to the examples in S0. The lists do not say whether Selank falls under S0.

side.text: Side-effect data are sparse. The study abstracts say little about harms. FDA flags a possible immune-reaction risk and says it lacks safety information in people.

items.text: the Russian abstracts do not list side effects of Selank itself. One study measured side effects with the UKU scale and reported fewer phenazepam side effects when Selank was added.

items.text: FDA says compounded selank acetate may cause immune reactions for some routes, because the peptide can clump and contain peptide impurities.

items.text: Selank acts on the GABA system in lab studies, like benzodiazepines. A 2021 review said drugs with GABA effects can bring abuse and withdrawal risks and should be tested for abuse potential before public access.

unconfirmed: Russia's state drug register (grls.rosminzdrav.ru) asks for a picture code before showing results, so Selank's register entry could not be opened. Its Russian status comes from a 2022 review.
The Russian-language studies were read only as PubMed abstracts; doses, length and side effects were not available.
UK (MHRA) and Australia's TGA register were not checked.
surprises: Selank is sold in the US as a supplement, but FDA lists it as a substance that may pose significant safety risks in compounding and says it lacks important safety information in people.
Almost all human data come from small Russian studies, several of which compared Selank with a benzodiazepine rather than a placebo.
